The molecular budget of a peatland can be derived using solid‐state 1H and 13C NMR, and that the molecular budget of a catchment is dominated by the oxidation of polysaccharides.
Solid‐state 13CNMR spectroscopy can be used to track the transit of organic carbon through an ecosystem.

the molecular composition of the organic matter in the ecosystem and its changes through the ecosystem and not the total amount of C that is lost as CO2 or CH4.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

peat accumulation in this system is a process that is dominated by the selective oxidation of the O‐alkyl component of the organic matter, which results in the preservation and accumulation of the C‐alkyl component.
the C‐C bond cleavage/depoymerisation of lignins is a key process in the long‐term C accumulation in peatlands.
polysaccharide is the major component of organic matter in the ecosystem, and it is lost as gases, while the lignin is preferentially retained and accumulates at depth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the molecular composition of the peatland ecosystem is determined by the relative proportions of lignin and polysaccharide in the biomass, the relative proportions of these two components are preserved through decomposition, and the relative proportions are altered by the selective removal of polysaccharide from the ecosystem.
the C budget for the Moor House ecosystem is dominated by the preferential loss of polysaccharides and the preferential preservation of lignin.
peatland C accumulation is dominated by lignin‐derived C, but that the C is derived from the breakdown of the lignin side chains, rather than the aromatic core.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular structure of organic matter in peatland soils is a key determinant of the long‐term storage of C, with lignin‐rich organic matter having the greatest potential to be retained.

a 13C‐solid state NMR approach can be used to quantify the molecular composition of organic matter through an ecosystem and to estimate the proportion of carbon that is retained or lost as CO2 or CH4.
13C‐C‐NMR spectroscopy is a powerful tool for the investigation of the molecular budget of a peatland, and the results can be used to inform models of C dynamics.
